answer: Do not fold the aggregate consultation numbers or the anonymous free-text sentiment into the heritage documentation system as structured CRM facts — the CRM has no class for an opinion, attitude, or survey response, and inventing one would violate Minimality. `search.py docs` shows the CRM's own stated scope is 'the curated, factual knowledge about the past at a human scale', built from E4 Period downward on 'coherent phenomena ... occurring in time and space'. A mailing-list exchange on Issue 580 (CRMsoc redefinition of scope, thread t1556) makes the boundary explicit: Francesco Beretta argues that 'social facts' — collective attitudes, conventions, how a group of people feels about an event — are 'grafted onto the spatio-temporal' but are not themselves the spatio-temporal facts CRMbase commits to ('CRMbase is concerned with objective spatio-temporal facts'), and that a separate model (CRMsoc) would be needed for that overlay. Issue 580's outcome record shows the SIG resolved in 2025 to discontinue CRMsoc in the form it had taken. So the one extension aimed at exactly this kind of data was shelved, not delivered — there is no CRM-family home for '58% opposed' or hundreds of anonymous comments about how a road would feel. Two candidate classes I checked and rejected: E54 Dimension (its scope note restricts it to a quantifiable property measured by a calibrated method on a thing, e.g. a weight or a date — a vote share among 1,340 unidentified respondents is not that), and E13 Attribute Assignment (it documents someone asserting one property of one object; it cannot represent an aggregated, anonymous, mixed-sentiment outcome across a public without manufacturing a fictitious assertor). What the model does support, and what I would keep, is the outer administrative shell: the consultation exercise itself is a real E7 Activity carried out by the trust (P14), that took place at the parkland (P7 took place at / P8 took place within), has a time-span (P4), was motivated by (P17) or used as its subject the road scheme — itself modellable as an E29 Design or Procedure, a 'documented plan for the execution of actions' — and produced a report that is a legitimate E31 Document (P70 documents the activity, P129 is about the road proposal). Inside that document, the percentages and quoted comments can sit as opaque text via P3 has note / P190 has symbolic content — recorded as the existence and content of a document, not decomposed into CRM particulars. That is the honest scope boundary: the trust can document that it ran a consultation and hold the report, but the CRM does not extend to modelling public sentiment as heritage fact.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Scope note restricts it to a quantifiable property of a thing measured by a calibrated method (weight, date, hammer price); an aggregated vote share across 1,340 unidentified respondents is not a calibrated measurement of the parkland or the road.

Models one identifiable actor asserting one property of one object; an anonymous, aggregated, mixed public sentiment has no single assertor and no single asserted property, so forcing it into E13 would fabricate an assertion nobody made.

This is the extension the SIG built specifically for the 'social overlay' on spatio-temporal events (collective attitudes, conventions). Issue 580's outcome record shows work on it was discontinued in 2025, so the CRM family currently has no delivered class for this kind of data.

The docs command truncates narrative snippets at ~300 chars and gives no chunk id, so I could not run `quote` against the docx scope note itself; I instead verified the same sentence via a thread message that quotes it verbatim (t1564), which does carry a checkable id. `quote` also caught a near-miss: my first guess at an id for the issue register text ('issue580' / '580') is not a valid quotable source, so that clause is cited as a plain string (existence-checked) rather than a verified quotation.
